result_text:
`git.refresh()` and `Git.refresh()` now invalidate the cached `version_info` on every `Git` instance, so it no longer returns a stale value after a refresh. The change is all in `git/cmd.py`.

I ran a quick check: read `version_info`, call `git.refresh()`, read it again, and pickle and unpickle the instance. That ran without errors. It only used one git binary, so I haven't exercised your CentOS case where the executable path changes. I also didn't run the test suite.

- **How it works:** `Git` now has a class-level token that `refresh` replaces each time. Each instance remembers the token that was current when it cached its version. When `version_info` is read and the tokens differ, it drops the cached value and runs `git version` again.
- **Pickling:** the new per-instance token is excluded from pickling alongside `_version_info`.
- **Docstring:** the `version_info` docstring now says the per-instance cache is cleared whenever `refresh` is called.

The token is also replaced when a refresh fails and the old executable is restored. In that case the next `version_info` read re-runs `git version` once.
